description: This plot illustrates the relationship between "Co-occurrence Number" and "ACC (%)" for six different methods: Base, FT, IKE, MEND, MEMIT, and ROME. The x-axis is labeled "Co-occurrence Number" and employs a logarithmic scale for values above zero, with major tick marks at 0, $10^1$, $10^2$, and $10^3$. The y-axis is labeled "ACC (%)" and uses a linear scale ranging from 60 to above 80, with major tick marks at intervals of 5 units (60, 65, 70, 75, 80). All six methods are represented by solid lines that exhibit an upward trend across four distinct data points along the x-axis. The "Base" method is depicted by a black line with circle markers, increasing steadily from approximately 61.2% at the first data point to 66.8% at the final data point, with intermediate values near 63.5% and 65.2%. The "FT" method, shown as a blue line with downward-pointing triangle markers, rises from roughly 62.4% to 68.3%, passing through 65.1% and 67.7%. The "IKE" method is a red line with upward-pointing triangle markers, increasing from about 64.5% to 70.2%, with intermediate points at 67.8% and 69.4%. The "MEND" method, represented by a brown line with diamond markers, starts at approximately 65.8%, rises to 71.3% and 73.4%, and ends at 73.9%. The "MEMIT" method is a purple line with pentagon markers, increasing from roughly 66.4% to 72.6%, with intermediate values at 70.1% and 71.3%. Finally, the "ROME" method is shown as a green line with square markers, starting at approximately 72.3%, increasing to 76.0% and 77.5%, and ending at 77.6%.
